subject: DataFortify – Subprocessor roster and audit evidence request
body:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Park <danielle@datafortify.com>; Mark Li <mark.li@finplatform.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick: subprocessor roster + supporting evidence for procurement review

Hi Danielle / Mark,

Hope you’re well. We’re progressing DataFortify through our procurement and security gate for the upcoming integration (DF-4782). Purchasing has asked for a current list of subprocessors and a few lightweight evidence items so we can finish the data flow review. Can you share: 

- A single CSV listing all subprocessors, processing purpose, country of processing, and whether they have access to cleartext customer data.
- Copies or a link to your latest SOC 2 Type II and any encryption/key management attestations.
- Any residency or on‑prem options for EU/US data (if applicable).

If possible, attach the CSV and SOC2 PDF — otherwise a secure Drive link works. We need this by EOD Thursday to keep our deployment timeline.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Ops | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

-----Original Message-----
From: Danielle Park <danielle@datafortify.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Li <mark.li@finplatform.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 12:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick: subprocessor roster + supporting evidence for procurement review

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for the ping. Attaching our current subprocessor roster (CSV) and the SOC2 Type II. Brief notes up front:

- Most subprocessors are third‑party cloud providers and telemetry vendors; none have access to decrypted customer prompt data unless explicitly requested by the customer under a managed service contract.
- We use KMS (AWS KMS) for keys; HSM backed for customer-managed keys.
- EU residency: we can route EU customers to our EU tenant in Frankfurt for an additional configuration fee.

I’ve attached: datafortify-subprocessors-2026.csv and SOC2-Type2-DataFortify-2025.pdf. Let me know if you need a redlined DPA or additional detail on specific vendors.

Best,
Danielle Park
Head of Security & Compliance | DataFortify
danielle@datafortify.com
Attachments: datafortify-subprocessors-2026.csv (text/csv), SOC2-Type2-DataFortify-2025.pdf (application/pdf)

-----Original Message-----
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Park <danielle@datafortify.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick: subprocessor roster + supporting evidence for procurement review

Hi Danielle —

Thanks for sending these over and for the quick summary. A couple of follow ups from our security/privacy side before procurement signs off: 

1) In the CSV a few entries are marked as "analytics-relay" and "temp-cache" with country listed as "global". Can you provide a more explicit country list per vendor (even if it’s multiple entries) and clarify whether any of those vendors replicate logs off‑region?

2) For the KMS/HSM statement: can you confirm whether customer tenant keys are always customer‑managed (BYOK) for our integration, or whether you will hold keys by default? If you hold keys, please include the KMS account region and ownership model.

3) Is the SOC2 report available behind a portal link (for our legal team) with evidence items (e.g., vendor contracts, key rotation logs) or do you prefer to share a redacted bundle? We prefer a portal link with viewer access if possible.

4) Finally, we have a small subset of enterprise customers who require a prohibition on cross‑border replication of telemetry. For any processor marked "telemetry", please state whether they perform cross‑border replication and whether you can disable that for a named customer.

If you can reply to the numbered items that will speed up our review — copying Aditya who will confirm KMS/keys details from an engineering perspective.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Privacy Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.com

-----Original Message-----
From: Danielle Park <danielle@datafortify.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Li <mark.li@finplatform.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 14:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick: subprocessor roster + supporting evidence for procurement review

Hi Rafael / Kim —

Thanks — answers inline below.

1) Attached CSV v2 replaces "global" entries with explicit jurisdictions where the subprocessors have active replicas. For your flagged vendors:
   - telemetry‑relay‑01: replicas in US (us‑east‑1), EU (eu‑central‑1). Replication can be restricted per customer for enterprise contracts.
   - tempcache‑svc: primary in US (us‑west‑2), backup in APAC (ap‑southeast‑1). Retention and replication parameters configurable on request.

2) By default we hold master keys in a DataFortify AWS account to simplify operations. For enterprise customers we offer BYOK where the customer supplies keys in their own KMS/HSM. For your planned integration we can enable BYOK — if you want that we’ll need a short statement in the DPA and confirmation on whether Redwood will rotate keys or maintain them.

3) SOC2 portal: yes — https://www.datafortify.com/soc2-report-portal — I can provision viewer links for your legal team (valid 30 days). We will provide a redacted evidence bundle if portal access is not an option.

4) Telemetry replication: per (1) — telemetry‑relay‑01 can be toggled to disable EU->US replication for a named customer under enterprise contract. Please flag which customers need this.

I’ve attached updated roster: datafortify-subprocessors-2026-v2.csv.

Best,
Danielle

-----Original Message-----
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Park <danielle@datafortify.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick: subprocessor roster + supporting evidence for procurement review

Danielle —

Appreciate the quick turn. Two final items so we can close the security checklist: 

- Please provision a SOC2 portal viewer link for our legal team (legal@redwood.com) and CC me. We’ll use it to validate the control scope (encryption, access reviews, change control).
- Confirm in writing that for BYOK: 1) keys are provisioned into our customer KMS account (Redwood tenant), 2) DataFortify will not retain plaintext or recorded copies of the key material, and 3) key rotation semantics (who rotates and how often) — a short paragraph in an email is fine.

If we get those two items by EOD Friday our procurement ops will mark DF-4782 as cleared.

Thanks —
Rafael

-----Original Message-----
From: Danielle Park <danielle@datafortify.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Li <mark.li@finplatform.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 14:38:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick: subprocessor roster + supporting evidence for procurement review

Rafael / team —

Portal link provisioned for legal@redwood.com: https://www.datafortify.com/soc2/portal/viewer?token=eyJ0eXAi... (expires 2026-11-29).

BYOK confirmation: 
- Keys can be generated in the customer KMS and never exported to DataFortify. DataFortify does not store plaintext key material.
- For enterprise BYOK we will accept a key ARN from your tenant and use that for encryption operations.
- Key rotation: Customer rotates per their KMS policy; DataFortify recommends rotation every 12 months for master keys. We will perform application‑level rewrapping on rotation if requested; DataFortify will not rotate customer keys without explicit consent.

Let me know if you want the short confirmation copied into a DPA addendum.

Thanks,
Danielle

-----
Action items (internal):
- Rafael: confirm whether Redwood will require BYOK for this account and prepare a short BYOK acceptance statement for the DPA.
- Kimberly: confirm procurement timeline and attach DF-4782 record to the Deal in HubSpot.
- Aditya: validate hostnames/regions for telemetry relay configuration (telemetry‑relay‑01) and confirm whether we need a runbook to toggle replication per customer.
